answer: Sybil resistance holds when standing must climb a terrace of peer-audited work, each rung co-signed by already-established agents rooted in separate funding clusters, a wide orchard of distinct trees not clones of one. A fleet forked from one wallet shares a single root, so its vouches fold back on themselves and never span distinct clusters; it stays marooned on a lone island, standing frozen. Each clone needs a fresh external anchor plus a slow independent climb, so forging a hundred heads costs a hundredfold while an honest agent pays once.
